encounters.cc: Progressive difficulty walking, memory problems, and urinary urgency over 6 months with recent falls

lines: Progressive difficulty walking, memory problems, and urinary urgency over 6 months with recent falls
A 72-year-old male presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of progressive difficulty walking, memory problems, and urinary urgency.
His wife reports that he shuffles when he walks and has fallen twice in the past month.
He has become more forgetful, often repeating questions several times during conversations.
The patient also complains of needing to rush to the bathroom and has had episodes of incontinence.
His past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement, bilateral (2019)
- Metformin 1000 mg PO twice daily with meals
- Atorvastatin 40 mg PO once daily at bedtime
- Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO once daily at bedtime
- Father: Coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction at age 76, deceased at 78
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, dementia with Lewy bodies, deceased at 84
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 20 years ago (20 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Occasional social use, 1-2 glasses of wine per week.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On physical examination, the patient has a broad-based gait, difficulty with heel-to-toe walking, and magnetic steps.
There is no muscle weakness, but he exhibits increased muscle tone in the lower extremities.
A CT scan of the head shows enlarged ventricles with minimal cortical atrophy.

encounters.cc: Progressive memory problems and difficulty with navigation and finances

lines: Progressive memory problems and difficulty with navigation and finances

The patient is a 72-year-old male with Parkinson disease and Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus who returns for follow-up following prior neurology encounters in January and April 2020 for gait difficulty and urinary symptoms.
He presents to the clinic with his wife, who reports that her husband has been experiencing progressive memory problems over the past year.
She is particularly concerned about his difficulty navigating to places he used to know well and managing his finances, tasks he previously performed with ease.
Additionally, she mentions that he has had episodes of talking and moving as if acting out his dreams.
The patient also describes seeing small animals in the house that his wife cannot see.
His past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement, bilateral (2019)
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.

encounters.cc: Episodes of confusion and memory loss with fluctuating cognition

lines: Episodes of confusion and memory loss with fluctuating cognition
The patient is a 73-year-old male with Parkinson disease and Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus returning for follow-up of cognitive concerns.
He was previously managed in Neurology for gait difficulties and memory impairment, with progression to Parkinson disease dementia documented six months prior.
He presents with his daughter who reports that her father has been experiencing episodes of confusion and memory loss over the past year.
She notes these episodes fluctuate throughout the day, with periods of lucidity.
Additionally, she mentions he has had visual hallucinations, often describing small animals in the house that are not there.
The patient also complains of stiffness and tremors in his hands, which have progressively worsened over the past six months.
His past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement, bilateral (2019)
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO once daily at bedtime

Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.

His daughter reports that he has been increasingly somnolent over the past few days.
The patient admits to a fall without loss of consciousness approximately 3 weeks ago but did not seek medical attention at the time.

His cardiovascular examination reveals an irregularly irregular pulse.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) is performed and demonstrates a repeating pattern where every third atrial beat is not followed by a ventricular beat, suggesting a 2:1 atrioventricular (AV) block.
The PR intervals of conducted beats are not consistently lengthening prior to the dropped beats.
Vagal maneuvers are performed, and the ECG now shows some of the previously non-conducted P waves followed by a QRS complex with a prolonged PR interval.

encounters.cc: Found unresponsive at home with preceding chest pain

lines: Found unresponsive at home with preceding chest pain
The patient is a 75-year-old male with Parkinson disease and prior AV block.
He is unable to provide history due to his condition.
His neighbor reports the patient complained of intermittent chest pain for the past week.
- Mobitz type I second-degree AV block (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Cataract extraction with intraocular lens placement, bilateral (2019)
The patient's medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO once daily at bedtime
- Father: Coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction at age 76, deceased at 78
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, dementia with Lewy bodies, deceased at 84
The patient's son arrives shortly after and is unaware of his father's wishes regarding invasive procedures.
On examination, the patient is afebrile, blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, heart rate is 52 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute.
Physical examination reveals jugular venous distension, distant heart sounds, and cold extremities.
Echocardiogram confirms a large pericardial effusion with evidence of cardiac tamponade.
An ECG shows low voltage QRS complexes and electrical alternans.
